title: At 3 interview turns, deep profile fields are rarely reached
detail: field-coverage.csv shows purpose_of_travel, nationality and residence_country supplied by most scenarios, but date_of_birth, passport_number, marital_status and dependants are seldom reached. The interview asks one question per turn, so a 3-turn budget covers only the opening of the profile. This is a property of the RUN CONFIGURATION, not of the product, and is stated here rather than left to look like product coverage.
remedy: Re-run with --turns 8+ for a deep-profile pass; cost scales roughly linearly with turns because each turn is one gpt-4o call.

title: Journey stages 2-6 unreachable by the guest identity the public funnel creates
detail: journey-coverage.csv: intake COVERED (107+ scenarios, results generated and persisted across reload); documents, narrative/generate, readiness, prefill and submission all NOT_COVERED. JwtGuard is fail-closed for anonymous identities and the public funnel only ever mints an anonymous one, so these stages need an authenticated fixture account that this run did not provision.
remedy: Provision a seeded test user and reuse the repo's existing Playwright auth fixture (playwright.config.ts already supports E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL / E2E_CONSULTANT_EMAIL storageState projects); point the harness at that storageState to cover stages 2-6.
resolution: Closed. Seeded an authenticated fixture user (qa.stage.fixture@example.invalid) directly in the local Supabase auth schema, confirmed handle_new_user populated public.users, and built qa/visaai-autonomous-e2e/harness/run-stages.mjs to log in through the real /en/login form and walk every gated stage. Result: documents, narrative/generate, readiness, prefill and submission are all reachable and render their expected content — 14 applications x 5 stages = 70 stage visits, 0 failures, 0 P0/P1.

title: Long runs were being reaped by the OS under memory pressure
detail: Two consecutive scenario runs were killed externally at ~336 and ~342 ledger rows. Diagnosed as host memory pressure (vm_stat showed ~65MB free with the Next dev server, NestJS API, the Supabase docker stack and N Chromium contexts all resident) rather than any product or harness logic error — the environment itself stayed healthy throughout (api 200, web 307, db 200) and the append-only ledger meant nothing was lost on either kill.
root_cause: worker() held ONE browser context for the entire run. A context accumulates cache, storage and service workers for every page it has ever opened, so its footprint grew monotonically across hundreds of scenarios.
fix: Recycle the browser context every 25 scenarios (CONTEXTS_RECYCLE_EVERY) and drop concurrency from 4 workers to 2. Keeps the footprint flat over a long run.
evidence: ledger resumed at exactly the last completed scenario after both kills — resumability verified twice under real interruption, which is precisely what the checkpointing requirement exists for.

title: Login silently failed because the fill raced React hydration
detail: A 14-run batch aborted at login. Evidence screenshot showed the password field populated but the EMAIL field empty, with no error message — the form had submitted with no email. Cause: filling the controlled input before hydration completed, after which hydration reset it. Fixed with a verify-after-fill helper that re-fills up to 5 times until inputValue() matches. This was a harness defect, not a product defect: a human types after the page settles.

title: All three previously-pending areas tested
uploads: 10 cases against the product's own rules (.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.heic/.pdf, 50MB cap): valid PDF, valid PNG, 1x1 tiny PNG, Unicode filename, 180-char filename, duplicate file, misleading extension (text bytes named .pdf), corrupt PDF — all ACCEPTED as designed; disallowed extension (.exe) and 53MB oversized file — both correctly REJECTED with a toast. 0 mismatches.
accessibility: axe-core WCAG 2.0/2.1 A+AA across 8 pages (marketing home, login, funnel entry, pricing, intake, documents, readiness, submission): ZERO violations. Validated as a real audit, not a no-op — a deliberately broken control page produced 5 violations (button-name, document-title, html-has-lang, image-alt, label) while the login page passed 29 rules with 0 violations and 0 incomplete.
payments: Presentation and gating only, by policy. No card details were entered and no checkout was completed, so no charge (real or test) could occur. Pricing page and readiness paywall both returned 0 server errors. Found FINDING-PRICING-001.
not_covered: Completing a checkout, entering card data, and webhook-driven entitlement changes remain untested — deliberately, as they require handling payment credentials.
